title: NEB Class 11 Mock Exam 02 — Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics

questions.prompt: Ribosomes are best described as the site of:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptides; they are non-membrane-bound organelles.

questions.prompt: The cell wall of a typical plant cell is composed mainly of:
questions.explanation: Plant walls are cellulose; chitin occurs in fungi and peptidoglycan in bacteria.

questions.prompt: Mucor, the black bread mould with coenocytic hyphae, is placed in which kingdom of the five-kingdom system?
questions.explanation: Mucor is a phycomycete fungus with chitinous walls and absorptive nutrition.

questions.prompt: Pinus produces seeds but no fruits because its ovules lie exposed on megasporophylls; it is therefore classified as a:
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms bear naked seeds on cone scales without an ovary wall.

questions.prompt: Mustard (Brassica campestris), a crop widely grown in Nepal, belongs to the angiosperm family:
questions.explanation: Brassica species are crucifers — family Brassicaceae with tetramerous flowers and tetradynamous stamens.

questions.prompt: The molecular mass of sulphuric acid, H₂SO₄, calculated from atomic masses (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16) is:
The number of molecules contained in 2 moles of a gas is approximately:
questions.explanation: N = n × Nₐ = 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.2044 × 10²⁴ molecules.

questions.prompt: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle places a fundamental limit on simultaneous measurement of position and momentum expressed as:
questions.explanation: The product of uncertainties can never fall below h/4π.

questions.prompt: The ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24), which violates the simple Aufbau prediction, is:
questions.explanation: A half-filled 3d⁵ subshell gains extra exchange stability, pulling one 4s electron down.

questions.prompt: According to VSEPR theory, the shape of the ammonia molecule NH₃ is:
questions.explanation: Three bond pairs plus one lone pair around nitrogen give a pyramidal geometry.

questions.prompt: If α and β are roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0, then the product αβ equals:
questions.explanation: Product of roots = c/a = 6/1 = 6 (indeed α = 2, β = 3).

questions.prompt: The quadratic equation whose roots are 2 and 3 is:
questions.explanation: Sum = 5, product = 6, so x² − (sum)x + product = x² − 5x + 6 = 0.

questions.prompt: The principal value branch (range) of cos⁻¹x is:
questions.explanation: Cosine inverse is defined on [−1, 1] with principal range [0, π].

questions.prompt: If tan θ = tan α, the general solution for θ is:
questions.explanation: Tangent repeats every π, giving θ = nπ + α; the ± form belongs to squared equations like tan²θ = tan²α.

questions.prompt: The arithmetic mean of the two numbers 4 and 16 is:
questions.explanation: AM = (4 + 16)/2 = 10; note GM would be 8 and HM 6.4.

questions.prompt: The cross product A × B of two parallel vectors has magnitude:
questions.explanation: |A × B| = AB sin θ vanishes at θ = 0° or 180°.

questions.prompt: For a body of mass m moving with speed v in a circle of radius r, the required centripetal force is:
questions.explanation: Newton's second law with centripetal acceleration v²/r gives F = mv²/r directed to the centre.

questions.prompt: The acceleration due to gravity at depth d below the Earth's surface (R = Earth's radius) becomes:
questions.explanation: Inside a uniform sphere only the mass within radius (R − d) attracts, giving linear decrease g′ = g(1 − d/R).

questions.prompt: The triple point of water, used to define the kelvin scale, lies at:
questions.explanation: Ice, liquid water and vapour coexist uniquely at 273.16 K and about 611.7 Pa.

questions.prompt: According to Newton's law of cooling, the rate of loss of heat of a hot body is directly proportional to:
options: The fourth power of its temperature
The excess of its temperature over surroundings
questions.explanation: dT/dt ∝ (T − T_s): cooling is fastest when the temperature difference is largest.
